Messages.Author: wastaz
Messages.Body:
> ...snip...
> But I've never seen either been used, so we decided against talking about it.
> ...snip...
>
Disclaimer, I haven't had time to watch this episode yet.
Anyway...

Actually, I'd see this as a great reason to actually -do- talk about it. It's all good and nice to talk about things that everyone knows about, ie. ashurs/liquidation. However the real interesting part should be talking about the corner case cards that isn't included in 50% of all tournament decks.

"Everyone" (stupid word, but you get what I mean (I hope)) knows about ashurs/liquidation and sudario refraction. I'd see this as a reason to talk -less- about those cards since you don't really watch this kind of show if you're not already pretty into the game (this is not a "vtes for newbies"-show after all  although maybe that would be a good idea...anyway...).

Here you have a forum to really show off your crazy ideas, interesting theories that might/might not work, cards that gets forgotten, and people will listen to you and start to think about doing interesting stuff. You could use this as a sort of "catalyst" for combatting deck building stagnation.

Sure, summon soul is horrible from a pure recursion view, but its inferior is "gain 2 pool". People play art scam, and that's just gain 2 pool and nothing else, so shouldn't summon soul in a way be "better"? (Ok, it requires NEC whereas art scam only requires a !TOR...)

tl;dr
Covering "mainstream" and "known combos" is good. But don't miss out on the "wonky sidelines" because if the entire vtes community suddenly decides that sudario or ashurs is the only viable recursion then we might be missing out on potential interesting deck ideas. Please don't just cover the trends, _be_ the trendsetters/inspiration for the trendsetters!

Messages.Author: Lambach
Messages.Body:
Hey guys. I am a big fan of your show (is it sad that the new C&E is a highlight of my week? Yes I think so).

Anyway, I am a mostly casual player who has played a few tourneys (I am part of a playtest group), so I've played alot of VTES but have some bad habits that your show is doing alot to help me inprove.

So you referred many times to "girls" decks in this episode, but did not actually discuss any "girls" decks. I know generally what sort of decks you are talking about and I have seen some in the TWDA, but with so many references to "girls" decks it would have been instructive to see you discuss 1 in depth. As is, I still find the recursion concept of deckbuilding difficult (I think that Infernal Pursuit variant would be ridiculously hard to play).

Sorry if I seem like a total noob, but maybe I am your target audience? A long time VTES player who is not so good but is trying to get better and trying to wrap his mind around more advanced concepts of this very difficult game.

Cheers. Look forward to the next episode.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body:
Wastaz. Summon Soul inferior gives 2 BLOOD, not pool. I wish it would be pool.

On another topic, I once had a really wacky deck that worked reasonably well at the time, crypt was basically Marcus Vitel advanced, Pochtli, and Carlotta. Idea was this, Marcus Vitel gets couple copies of Legion, and makes like half a dozen or so fledglings from dominate skill cards, which in the process pretty much dumps your whole library to your ashheap, and then you use Pochtli and Carlotta to get back the cards you want to use from there. Hopefully your prey had camarilla vampire so all the fledglings get +1 bleed from Marcus, either way, have someone play psychic veil and then they all bleed with as many governs as you can fetch back, which were used early game by Marcus to get Pochtli and Carlotta in the play cheap.

Now that deck was years ago, now you could probably make it hell of a lot better by adding ashur tablets there, so then after you have dumped your whole library, you fetch the ashurs back and then pop them to get back dozen cards that you need to oust your prey.
